raw_case_text:
A 65-year-old male with hypertension and atrial fibrillation was admitted to the University of Rochester Medical Center with fever, chest pain, and dyspnea. A CT Chest angiogram revealed bilateral ground-glass opacities with mediastinal lymphadenopathy and no embolic disease. He was admitted to the general medicine service and was treated for community-acquired pneumonia with ceftriaxone and doxycycline. His fevers persisted for the first three days. On hospital day 6 his antimicrobial therapy was broadened to vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and azithromycin due to worsening hypoxia and was continued for 10 days. He was found to be HIV positive with a RNA level greater than 500,000 copies/ml and a CD4 count of 15. On hospital day 9 he required intubation for worsening hypoxia. He underwent bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) with pneumocystis jiroveci identified on PCR testing and microscopy and CMV was identified on viral cell culture. Sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim and glucocorticoid therapy was empirically started and he completed 21 days of therapy.
On hospital day 23 he was extubated. Due to increasing lethargy he was reintubated on hospital day 27 for airway protection. After intubation he developed intermittent fevers for 25 days with altered mental status. Vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam were restarted. An initial work up for encephalopathy was performed with normal ammonia (18 mumol/L), normal CT head with and without contrast, and negative evaluation for infection including blood, urine, tracheal aspirate, and stool cultures. An electroencephalogram was performed and showed moderate encephalopathy without epileptiform abnormalities. Highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) with elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide was started on hospital day 33 after HIV genotype testing returned. There was concern for drug fever from dexmedetomidine and piperacillin-tazobactam and both drugs were discontinued on hospital day 32 and 37. After no improvement in fevers a MRI of the head with and without contrast was performed on hospital day 37 and showed acute infarcts in the bilateral thalami, right parietal lobe, and right basal ganglia. Neurology felt it was embolic phenomena from atrial fibrillation. He also developed persistent, nonbloody loose stools with negative bacterial and parasite stool studies so serum CMV PCR was checked on hospital day 43 showing 2,623,108 IU/mL. With new nuchal rigidity on exam and right lower extremity weakness a lumbar puncture was performed on hospital day 44 after another head CT was normal. Spinal fluid analysis was consistent with encephalitis and CSF PCR for CMV DNA was positive (Table 1). After serum CMV PCR positivity returned ganciclovir was started on hospital day 47. MRI imaging of the cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine showed extensive linear leptomeningeal enhancement along the lower spinal cord, conus medullaris, and roots of the cauda equine with thickening of the roots concerning for radiculomyelitis (Figure 1). At this point his mental status remained poor with quadriparesis and flaccid paraplegia. He underwent tracheostomy on hospital day 50.
Serum CMV DNA PCR and HIV RNA PCR were checked weekly to monitor treatment efficacy, and both decreased significantly on treatment (Table 2). No further lumbar punctures were performed. He received 30 days of IV ganciclovir 469mg twice daily before decreasing to IV ganciclovir 469mg daily after two consecutive weeks of undetectable serum CMV DNA PCR, hospital day 76. He received IV ganciclovir daily for 85 days total, before switching to oral valganciclovir 900mg daily. The serum HIV RNA PCR continued to decline and was 49 copies/mL on hospital day 128 (96 days after initiation of HAART therapy). He remained on mechanical ventilation and was able to move his upper extremities with assistance and could answer simple questions. He never regained function in his lower extremities. After minimal improvement he opted to stop mechanical ventilation and passed away on hospital day 147.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 65-year-old male with hypertension and atrial fibrillation presented with fever, chest pain, and dyspnea, and following treatment for HIV-associated Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia developed persistent fevers, loose stools, encephalopathy, nuchal rigidity, and progressive quadriparesis/paraplegia from cytomegalovirus encephalitis and radiculomyelitis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was initially admitted to the general medicine service with fever, chest pain, and dyspnea and failed empiric ceftriaxone/doxycycline (days 1–5) and vancomycin/piperacillin-tazobactam/azithromycin (days 6–15). He was newly diagnosed with advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 count 15 cells/μL, HIV RNA >500,000 copies/mL), intubated on hospital day 9 for worsening hypoxia, and diagnosed via BAL with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and CMV co-isolation. He completed 21 days of trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and glucocorticoids and was extubated on day 23, but required re-intubation on day 27 for progressive lethargy. Thereafter, he experienced 25 days of persistent intermittent fevers, altered mental status, nonbloody loose stools, nuchal rigidity, and progressive quadriparesis/flaccid paraplegia despite initiating elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide on day 33.
subjective.past_medical_history: Hypertension; atrial fibrillation; newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 count 15 cells/μL, HIV RNA >500,000 copies/mL).
subjective.review_of_systems: Initial admission positive for fever, chest pain, and dyspnea; late hospital course (day 27 onward) positive for lethargy, persistent fever, nonbloody diarrhea, neck stiffness, and progressive four-limb weakness.

objective.physical_examination: Initial course marked by progressive hypoxemia requiring intubation on day 9. Late course (days 27–50): Persistent fevers, severe encephalopathy, nuchal rigidity, right lower extremity weakness progressing to quadriparesis and flaccid paraplegia, requiring re-intubation (day 27) and tracheostomy (day 50).
objective.routine_investigations: Initial HIV workup: HIV-positive with plasma HIV RNA >500,000 copies/mL (declining to 49 copies/mL on hospital day 128). Day 27–44 encephalopathy and diarrhea workup: Normal serum ammonia (18 μmol/L); negative blood, urine, tracheal aspirate, and stool bacterial/parasitic cultures; non-contrast/contrast head CTs normal; EEG showed moderate diffuse encephalopathy without epileptiform discharges; day 43 serum CMV DNA PCR markedly elevated at 2,623,108 IU/mL (becoming undetectable by day 76 after IV ganciclovir).
objective.advanced_workup: Baseline CD4+ T-cell count: 15 cells/μL. Admission CT chest angiogram: Bilateral ground-glass opacities and mediastinal lymphadenopathy without pulmonary embolism. Day 9 bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL): Positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii by both PCR and microscopy, and positive for cytomegalovirus (CMV) by viral cell culture. Day 37 brain MRI: Acute cardioembolic infarcts in the bilateral thalami, right parietal lobe, and right basal ganglia. Day 44 lumbar puncture and spine MRI: CSF profile consistent with encephalitis with positive CSF CMV DNA PCR; contrast-enhanced cervical, thoracic, and lumbar spine MRI demonstrated extensive linear leptomeningeal enhancement along the lower spinal cord, conus medullaris, and thickened cauda equina nerve roots diagnostic of CMV radiculomyelitis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Newly diagnosed advanced HIV/AIDS (CD4 count 15 cells/μL) complicated initially by severe Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (confirmed by BAL microscopy and PCR) and subsequently by severe cytomegalovirus (CMV) meningoencephalitis and lumbosacral radiculomyelitis (confirmed by CSF CMV DNA PCR, serum CMV viral load 2,623,108 IU/mL, and conus medullaris/cauda equina leptomeningeal enhancement on spine MRI) plus cardioembolic cerebral infarcts from atrial fibrillation. Plan and clinical course: Completed a 21-day course of trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and glucocorticoids for PJP and started HAART (elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide) on day 33. Following confirmation of CMV encephalitis/radiculomyelitis, intravenous ganciclovir (469 mg BID for 30 days, then 469 mg daily for 85 total IV days before transitioning to oral valganciclovir 900 mg daily) cleared his serum CMV viremia by day 76 and suppressed HIV RNA to 49 copies/mL by day 128; however, due to persistent ventilator dependence and irreversible paraplegia, the patient elected terminal ventilator withdrawal and died on hospital day 147.
